Lexicon Latīnitātis Cotīdiānae
Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Household, washing & chores

stain noun and verb

also stains, stained, a dirty mark, spot (a stain), get dirty, soil

classical

Paul. ex Fest. p. 121 Müll.: lābēs macula in vestīmentō dīcitur (Lewis & Short, s.v. lābēs)

macula, maculae f.

noun, first declension

a stain, a spot, a mark

The plain word for a spot or stain; also the spots of an animal’s coat, the mesh of a net and, by a figure, a disgrace (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • inquinō, inquināre, inquināvī, inquinātum — stain, soil, get dirty

    verb, first conjugation · classical · Plaut. Capt. 2.2.17: vestem (Lewis & Short); Cato Agr. 65.1

    The everyday verb for dirtying clothes, hands, food; also, by a figure, to corrupt.

  • lābēs, lābis f. — a stain, a blot

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Ov. Ars 1.514: sine lābe toga (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 2.1.235 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Hor., Ov.; also post-Augustan prose)

    In Cicero only by a figure: a stain on one’s name (Lewis & Short). A different word from lābēs, a fall.

  • maculō, maculāre, maculāvī, maculātum — stain, spot

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Catull. 63.7: solum sanguine (Lewis & Short)

    Chiefly of blood and, by a figure, of guilt (caede maculātus, Cic. Rep. 2.46); for everyday dirt, inquināre.

Examples

  • sī inquināta erit, lavātō ā foliīs et stercore pūrgātō

    if it is dirty, wash it and clean off the leaves and muckCato Agr. 65.1

  • Cavē nē vestem inquinēs.

    Mind you don’t stain your clothes.composed

See also dirty, laundry.
